He was a local lord ([[:en:Kokujin|Kokujin]]) of {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}}, serving as the lord of {{ill|Takatō Castle|de|Burg Takatō|es|Castillo de Takatō|fa|قلعه تاکاتوئو|fr|Château de Takatō|ja|高遠城|ko|다카토성|ml|ടകറ്റോ കാസിൽ|zh|高遠城|qid=Q11672954|lt=Takato Castle}} (located in present-day {{ill|Ina, Nagano|ar|إنا (ناغانو)|azb|اینا، ناقانو|ce|Ина (гӀала)|ceb|Ina (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Ina (Nagano)|es|Ina (Nagano)|fa|اینا، ناگانو|fi|Ina (Nagano)|fr|Ina (Nagano)|gl|Ina|hy|Ինա (քաղաք)|id|Ina, Nagano|it|Ina (Nagano)|ja|伊那市|ko|이나시|mzn|اینا، ناگانو|nl|Ina (Nagano)|pl|Ina (miasto)|pt|Ina (Nagano)|ro|Ina|ru|Ина (город)|sv|Ina, Nagano|tg|Ина|th|อินะ|tl|Ina, Nagano|tr|Ina, Nagano|tt|Ина (шәһәр)|uk|Іна (Наґано)|ur|اینا، ناگانو|uz|Ina (Nagano)|vi|Ina, Nagano|war|Ina, Nagano|zh|伊那市|zh_classical|伊那市|zh_min_nan|Ina-chhī|zh_yue|伊那|qid=Q840888|lt=Ina, Nagano}}, {{ill|Takatō, Nagano|fa|تاکاتوئو، ناگانو|ja|高遠町|ko|다카토정|qid=Q7677451|lt=Takato Town}}). As a retainer of the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|甲斐武田氏}}, he held the position of {{ill|Sakikata-shū|ja|信濃先方衆}} in charge of the Shinano frontlines. He belonged to the {{ill|Q11672957|ja|高遠氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takato clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11672957}}, a cadet branch of the {{ill|Suwa clan|en|Suwa clan|qid=Q2975376|lt=Suwa clan}}, and sometimes used the Suwa surname. His official titles included Shinano-no-Kami and Kii-no-Kami. Yoritsugu was the son and heir of Takato Mitsunari (Shinano-no-Kami) and married the daughter of {{ill|Suwa Yorimitsu|en|Suwa Yorimitsu|qid=Q7650544|lt=Suwa Yorimitsu (Aki-no-Kami)}}.

== Biography ==
Yoritsugu is said to have been the son or grandson of {{ill|Takato Tsugimune|ja|高遠継宗}}, who opposed the Suwa main family during internal conflicts. After {{ill|Q11631959|ja|諏訪頼満|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Yorimitsu (Aki-no-Kami)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11631959}} unified the Suwa clan, Yoritsugu initially resisted but eventually became a vassal and married Yorimitsu’s daughter.

During the Sengoku period, the Takeda clan of {{ill|Kai Province|en|Kai Province|qid=Q858076|lt=Kai Province}} and the Suwa clan of Shinano Province had a long-standing alliance. However, in Tenbun 10 (1542), {{ill|Takeda Shingen|ja|武田晴信|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeda Harunobu (Shingen)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田信玄|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q276404}} (later known as Takeda Shingen) ascended as the Takeda clan head and began an aggressive campaign to conquer Shinano, breaking the alliance and invading the Suwa domain. On {{ill|July 2|en|July 2|qid=Q2697|lt=July 2}}, Tenbun 11 (1542), Yoritsugu assisted the Takeda in attacking {{ill|Uehara Castle|ja|上原城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uehara Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11358576}}, the base of {{ill|Suwa Yorishige|en|Suwa Yorishige|qid=Q1213900|lt=Suwa Yorishige}}, who surrendered to the Takeda. Yorishige was taken to {{ill|Q11577765|ja|甲府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11577765}} and forced to commit suicide later that month. The Suwa domain was divided between the Takeda and Yoritsugu, with Yoritsugu controlling the western half.

Yoritsugu, aiming to restore the Suwa clan's authority, allied with {{ill|Q11624578|ja|藤沢頼親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujisawa Yorichika|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11624578}} of {{ill|Q11591217|ja|福与城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuyo Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11591217}} in {{ill|Ina district|ja|伊那郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina District, Nagano|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11380911}} to invade Takeda territory. However, on {{ill|September 25|en|September 25|qid=Q2886|lt=September 25}}, he was defeated in the {{ill|Battle of Miyagawa|ja|宮川の戦い|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Miyagawa (1542)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17214872}} and forced to retreat from the Suwa region.

In Tenbun 14 (1545), Takeda forces attacked the allied Fujisawa Yorichika and {{ill|Ōi Sadataka|ja|大井貞隆|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōi Sadataka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11432233}} of {{ill|Q11653547|ja|長窪城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagakubo Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11653547}}. Takato Castle fell to the Takeda on {{ill|April 17|en|April 17|qid=Q2520|lt=April 17}}, and Yoritsugu surrendered, traveling to Kōfu to submit to Takeda authority. After the castle’s capture, the Takeda fortified Takato Castle as a strategic base for controlling Shinano.

In Tenbun 17 (1548), after the Takeda’s defeat at the {{ill|Battle of Uedahara|en|Battle of Uedahara|qid=Q1358091|lt=Battle of Uedahara}} against {{ill|Murakami Yoshikiyo|en|Murakami Yoshikiyo|qid=Q1048622|lt=Murakami Yoshikiyo}}, unrest spread in Takeda-controlled territories. Yoritsugu returned to Takato Castle on {{ill|April 3|en|April 3|qid=Q2509|lt=April 3}} (as noted in the *Kōhakusai-ki*). 

Yoritsugu continued serving the Takeda but was reportedly forced to commit suicide during a campaign in {{ill|Minami Shinshū area|ja|下伊那|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimoinadani|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 南信州地域|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11666112}} in Tenbun 21 (1552). His posthumous name was 大用普徹大禅定院 (Daiyō Futtetsu Daizendō-in). Following his death, {{ill|Hoshina Masatoshi|en|Hoshina Masatoshi|qid=Q2040645|lt=Hoshina Masatoshi}}, a vassal of the Takato clan, rose to prominence under the Takeda. While traditionally believed to mark the Takato clan's extinction, recent studies suggest that {{ill|Takeda Katsuyori|en|Takeda Katsuyori|qid=Q662482|lt=Takeda Katsuyori}}, Takeda Shingen's fourth son, inherited the Takato-Suwa lineage.<ref>Marushima Kazuhiro, "Kōyasan Jōkei-in's *Kōkoku Kako-chō*: The *Past Records of Kōshū Monthly Memorials*," *Takeda Clan Studies,* No. 34, 2006.</ref>
